title: Roadless Areas within B.C.'s Ecoregions
summary: The amount and distribution of roadless land vary considerably across British Columbia. Explore the share of each terrestrial ecoregion that lies more than 500 metres from a road.
sourceNote: Environmental Reporting BC calculated roadless area from the B.C. Digital Road Atlas accessed May 1, 2018. Roadless means more than 500 metres from a road. This project preserves the 43 ecoregion geometries and reported percentages embedded in the Province's May 2018 interactive map; results are a coarse-scale snapshot and are reported to three significant figures.
details: Twenty-seven of B.C.'s 43 terrestrial ecoregions are more than 50 percent roadless, while six have less than 25 percent roadless area.
Ecoregions with high population densities and larger road networks have the lowest shares. Lower Mainland, Georgia-Puget Basin, and Okanogan Highland each have 13 percent roadless area.
Point to an ecoregion to see its percentage, or click or tap it to keep that ecoregion selected.

scenes.label: Distribution
scenes.title: Two thirds of B.C.'s landbase is roadless
scenes.text: Across the province, approximately 62.6 million hectares—66 percent of the landbase—lies more than 500 metres from a road. The distribution is uneven, from heavily roaded southern regions to large roadless northern and coastal landscapes.

callout.label: Province-wide
callout.detail: Approximately 62.6 million hectares in the 2018 indicator.

scenes.label: More roadless
scenes.title: Twenty-seven ecoregions are more than half roadless
scenes.text: Most ecoregions remain predominantly roadless. The darkest greens show where more than three quarters of the land is beyond the indicator's 500-metre road influence zone.

callout.label: Predominantly roadless
callout.detail: Nearly two thirds of the terrestrial ecoregions.

scenes.label: More roaded
scenes.title: Six ecoregions have less than one quarter roadless
scenes.text: The lowest roadless shares occur in more populated and road-dense ecoregions. Eastern Vancouver Island, the Southern Rocky Mountain Trench, and the Thompson-Okanagan Plateau are among the six below 25 percent.

callout.label: Lowest band
callout.detail: All occur in the more roaded southern portion of the province.

scenes.label: Thirteen percent
scenes.title: Three ecoregions are only 13 percent roadless
scenes.text: Lower Mainland, Georgia-Puget Basin, and Okanogan Highland each have the lowest reported share. Their dense settlement, transportation, and resource-road networks leave comparatively little land beyond 500 metres from a road.
scenes.focus: Lower Mainland · Georgia-Puget Basin · Okanogan Highland
